messages:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] rollout 2026-03-21T20:12:56Z — safety-throttle triggered for release 3.10.1. Canary p95 = 2.38s (>2.2s). Action taken: reduce canary to 25%. Recommendation: automated rollback to last stable variant. /deploy status 6821 :warning:

alice: saw this. which exact change caused the spike? kernel flag or model micro-release? :eyes:

ben: it's the kernel selector change + small quantization tweak — variant v3.10.1-dedicated rolled into canary. logs show KV cache miss spikes right after request 1.4M.

carla: reproducing locally with the same traffic profile — kv-cache pressure goes up with longer prompts. not convinced full auto-rollback is the least disruptive.

product-qa: flagged two failing user flows from canary sessions (embedding latency + truncated responses). tagging ticket T-9241.

danny: quick idea: instead of full rollback, we can pin canary to v3.10.0-compat (micro-kernel downgrade) and re-route 60% of canary traffic to that variant while keeping 40% on 3.10.1 for metrics. less churn for customers.

alice: that sounds reasonable. what commands do we use to enact partial pin? I can do the operator handoff.

ben: deploy CLI: `deploy rollout 6821 --pin-variant v3.10.0-compat --traffic-split 60:40 --scope canary-usw` — but needs manual override of safety latch: `--force-override` and operator signoff.

carla: will also push a config tweak to bump kv-cache-size on the canary pool (small patch). that might help while we observe.

deploy-bot: note: manual override required. automated rollback will trigger in 5m unless an operator acknowledges. See /deploy acknowledge 6821 --user <name>.

alice: @danny can you take the override and pin? I'll draft a release-note patch describing temporary pin + follow-up perf investigation.

danny: taking it. `/deploy acknowledge 6821 --user danny && deploy rollout 6821 --pin-variant v3.10.0-compat --traffic-split 60:40 --scope canary-usw --force-override` executing now. :hammer_and_wrench:

product-qa: once done please update the customer-release-notes entry and add a line in the scheduled comms: "We observed a canary latency regression; routing adjusted while we investigate — no expected user impact."

ben: monitoring: i'll watch p95, error-rate, and kv-cache hit rate. If metrics improve in 10m we can resume rollout. if not, escalate to full rollback.

carla: patch applied to kv-cache config as well. keeping logs verbose for 30m.

alice: thanks team. decision: manual intervention -> pin canary to v3.10.0-compat, hold global rollout, update release notes and open follow-up RCA. I'll file a short ops summary into T-9241. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: acknowledge received from danny. safety-latch overridden. canary traffic rebalanced. Automated rollback cancelled for this window.

product-qa: added customer note and linked T-9241. will notify CSMs if we flip to a full rollback.

ben: keeping an eye. will call for rollback if p95 stays >2.2s after 15m.

alice: closing thread for now, will re-open if metrics degrade. thanks. :white_check_mark:
